reader.requirement: At 85 the pseudo-text delimiter == is a separator in COPY REPLACING and REPLACE: an opening == must be immediately preceded by a space and a closing == immediately followed by a space, comma, semicolon or period, else the source is refused; == outside balanced pairs delimiting pseudo-text (an unclosed pseudo-text, a stray == in a statement) is refused; == inside a nonnumeric literal is literal content.
reader.edition-search: grep Edition|dialectLevel|CobolVersion in CopyProcessor.cs: the only edition reads are OnNonPseudoTextOperand (the 2023 removal of non-pseudo-text COPY operands), the REPLACE scope and result-layout rules; ReadOperand's two delimiter checks (OperandScreen.Delimiter, COBOL2573), its no-closing-delimiter error and TextWord.TryNext's == recognition read no edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f03_01 covers legal placements (closing followed by comma, semicolon, period; opening at the start of a continuation line) and == inside a literal; the refusal half (opening not preceded by a space, closing followed by another character, unbalanced or stray ==) and COPY REPLACING are not exercised

citations.check: OK  §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR6  (4.2.1 Separators)  the text is in SR6

reader.notes: ReadOperand checks both placements for every pseudo-text operand of COPY and REPLACE at every edition; the 1985 text and the 2023 one state the same rule. The COBOL2573 message cites §2023:8.3.5 6) even at --std 85, a citation-only blemish, not a behaviour difference.

refuter.evidence: At --std 85: p6comma.cob (REPLACE ==XX1== BY ==AAA==,==XX2== ...) refused COBOL2573 'the opening == follows ',' with no space'; p6empty.cob REPLACE ==XX1 OF== BY ====. (empty pseudo-text, closing delimiter with no preceding space, legal by SR8) compiles and prints [AAA] (MATCH); p6semi.cob closing == followed by ';' then a second pair on the next line, MATCH AAAAAA; p6end.cob stray == after REPLACE OFF refused COBOL0001. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR6  (4.2.1 Separators)  the text is in SR6' (quote 'Pseudo-text delimiters may appear only in balanced pairs').
